questions.sec: Presenting parts of the fetal skull & head attitude
questions.q: Which statement about fetal skull diameters is stated as ALWAYS true?
opts: AP and transverse diameters are equal
Transverse diameter exceeds AP only in brow presentation
questions.exp: The notes open with the rule: AP diameter is always greater than transverse diameter. (Book p490)

questions.sec: Presenting parts of the fetal skull & head attitude
questions.q: Match the part of skull with its boundaries – Vertex : Brow : Face.
opts: Anterior to posterior fontanelle : anterior fontanelle to root of nose : root of nose to chin
Root of nose to chin : anterior to posterior fontanelle : anterior fontanelle to root of nose
Anterior fontanelle to root of nose : anterior to posterior fontanelle : root of nose to chin
Occiput to root of nose : anterior fontanelle to chin : root of nose to mentum
questions.exp: Vertex lies between anterior (diamond) and posterior (triangular) fontanelle; brow between anterior fontanelle and root of nose; face from root of nose to chin (mentum). (Book p490)

questions.sec: Presenting parts of the fetal skull & head attitude
questions.q: Fill in the shapes: the anterior fontanelle is ______ and the posterior fontanelle is ______, lying above the ______ lobe.
questions.exp: Anterior fontanelle is diamond-shaped; posterior fontanelle is triangular and lies above the occipital lobe. (Book p490)

questions.sec: Presenting parts of the fetal skull & head attitude
questions.q: In anencephaly the most common presenting part is ______, and face presentation is most commonly seen in ______.
questions.exp: Face is the m/c presenting part in anencephaly, and anencephaly is the m/c association of face presentation. (Book p490)

questions.sec: Presenting parts of the fetal skull & head attitude
questions.q: Normally the fetus in utero keeps all body parts in which attitude?
questions.exp: Normally the fetus in utero has all body parts flexed. (Book p490)

questions.sec: Presenting parts of the fetal skull & head attitude
questions.q: Match the position of fetal head to the presenting part – Flexed : Deflexed (neutral) : Partial extension : Full extension.
questions.exp: Flexed = vertex (m/c); deflexed/neutral = vertex; partial extension = brow; full extension = face. (Book p490)

questions.sec: Presenting parts of the fetal skull & head attitude
questions.q: Fill up: The vertex is bounded in front by the anterior fontanelle, behind by the posterior fontanelle and on each side by the ______.
questions.exp: The vertex is the quadrangular area between the two fontanelles and the two parietal eminences; it is the presenting area in a well-flexed head. (Book p490)

questions.sec: Sutures, fontanelles & skull terminology
questions.q: Identify the suture: the one running between the two frontal bones in the fetal skull is the ______.
questions.exp: The frontal (metopic) suture lies between the two frontal bones. (Book p490)

questions.sec: Sutures, fontanelles & skull terminology
questions.q: Match the suture with its location – Sagittal : Coronal : Lambdoid.
opts: Between the two parietal bones : between frontal and parietal bones : between parietal and occipital bone
Between frontal and parietal : between two parietals : between two frontals
Between parietal and occipital : between two parietals : between frontal and parietal
Between two frontals : between parietal and occipital : between frontal and parietal
questions.exp: Sagittal suture separates the parietal bones, coronal separates frontal from parietal, lambdoid separates parietal from occipital. (Book p490)

questions.sec: Sutures, fontanelles & skull terminology
questions.q: The anterior fontanelle is also known as ______ and the posterior fontanelle as ______.
questions.exp: Anterior fontanelle = bregma; posterior fontanelle = lambda. (Book p490)

questions.sec: Sutures, fontanelles & skull terminology
questions.q: Fontanelles are defined as ______ and at birth ______ fontanelles are present.
questions.exp: Fontanelles are gaps between suture lines; 6 are present at birth. (Book p490)

questions.sec: Sutures, fontanelles & skull terminology
questions.q: Match the terminology – Occiput : Sub-occiput : Mentum : Submentum.
opts: Occipital bone : below occiput : chin : below chin where face and neck meet
Below occiput : occipital bone : below chin : chin
Occipital bone : below chin : chin : neck
Highest point on sagittal suture : below occiput : chin : nose
questions.exp: Occiput = occipital bone; sub-occiput = below occiput; mentum = chin; submentum = below chin where face and neck meet. (Book p491)

questions.sec: Sutures, fontanelles & skull terminology
questions.q: Complete the terminology: Vertex is the ______; Frontal is any point on the ______; Bregma is any point on the ______.
opts: Highest point on sagittal suture; frontal suture; anterior fontanelle
Highest point on coronal suture; sagittal suture; posterior fontanelle
Lowest point on sagittal suture; frontal bone; anterior fontanelle
Highest point on lambdoid suture; frontal suture; posterior fontanelle
questions.exp: Vertex = highest point on sagittal suture; frontal = any point on frontal suture; bregma = any point on anterior fontanelle. (Book p491)

questions.sec: Sutures, fontanelles & skull terminology
questions.q: Match the suture with what it lies between — 1) Sagittal suture 2) Coronal suture 3) Lambdoid suture … A) The two parietal bones, with the posterior fontanelle at its posterior end B) The frontal and the two parietal bones, with the anterior fontanelle at the junction C) The two parietal bones and the occipital bone
questions.exp: The sagittal suture ends behind at the posterior fontanelle, the anterior fontanelle sits where the sagittal, coronal and frontal sutures meet. (Book p491)

questions.sec: Diameters of the fetal skull & engaging diameters
questions.q: The six AP diameters of the fetal skull listed in the notes are: sub-occipito-bregmatic, sub-occipito-frontal, occipito-frontal, mento-vertical and which two others?
questions.exp: The listed AP diameters: sub-occipito-bregmatic, sub-occipito-frontal, occipito-frontal, mento-vertical, sub-mento-bregmatic and sub-mento-vertical. (Book p491)

questions.sec: Diameters of the fetal skull & engaging diameters
questions.q: The longest AP diameter of the fetal skull is the ______, measuring ______, seen in ______ presentation.
questions.exp: Mento-vertical (14 cm) is the longest AP diameter, seen in brow presentation. (Book p491)

questions.sec: Diameters of the fetal skull & engaging diameters
questions.q: Because the mento-vertical diameter cannot pass the maternal pelvis, brow presentation requires:
questions.exp: The 14 cm mento-vertical diameter cannot pass the maternal pelvis, so C-section is required. (Book p491)

questions.sec: Diameters of the fetal skull & engaging diameters
questions.q: The two SECOND-longest AP diameters (each 11.5 cm) are:
questions.exp: Sub-mento-vertical and occipito-frontal both measure 11.5 cm – second longest. (Book p491)

questions.sec: Diameters of the fetal skull & engaging diameters
questions.q: Arrange the transverse diameters from smallest to longest with their values:
opts: Bimastoid 7.5 cm < bitemporal 8 cm < super sub-parietal 8.5 cm < biparietal 9.5 cm
Bitemporal 7.5 cm < bimastoid 8 cm < biparietal 8.5 cm < super sub-parietal 9.5 cm
Bimastoid 8 cm < bitemporal 8.5 cm < biparietal 9.5 cm < super sub-parietal 10 cm
Biparietal 7.5 cm < super sub-parietal 8 cm < bitemporal 8.5 cm < bimastoid 9.5 cm
questions.exp: Bimastoid (7.5) → bitemporal (8) → super sub-parietal (8.5) → biparietal (9.5 cm). (Book p491)

questions.sec: Diameters of the fetal skull & engaging diameters
questions.q: The most common engaging transverse diameter of the fetal skull is:
questions.exp: BPD (9.5 cm) is the m/c engaging diameter. (Book p491)

questions.sec: Diameters of the fetal skull & engaging diameters
questions.q: Match the vertex attitude to its engaging diameter – Fully flexed : Deflexed.
questions.exp: Fully flexed vertex engages by sub-occipito-bregmatic (9.5 cm); deflexed vertex by occipito-frontal (11.5 cm). (Book p491)

questions.sec: Diameters of the fetal skull & engaging diameters
questions.q: A fully extended head (face presentation) engages by which diameter(s)?
questions.exp: Face (fully extended) engages by sub-mento-vertical 11.5 cm or sub-mento-bregmatic 9.5 cm; brow (partially extended) by mento-vertical 14 cm. (Book p491)

questions.sec: Diameters of the fetal skull & engaging diameters
questions.q: 'Lightening' refers to:
opts: Relief of breathing symptoms as the fetal head descends into the pelvis
The sudden onset of regular, painful uterine contractions
Rupture of the membranes before labour has begun
Effacement of the cervix during the last week of pregnancy
questions.exp: Lightening is the relief of pressure symptoms when the presenting part descends, usually late in the third trimester. (Book p491)

questions.sec: Diameters of the fetal skull & engaging diameters
questions.q: Fill up: With a well-flexed head, the engaging diameter is the suboccipito-bregmatic at about ______ cm, whereas the occipito-frontal diameter measures about ______ cm.
questions.exp: Good flexion substitutes the shorter suboccipito-bregmatic (9.5 cm) diameter for the longer occipito-frontal (11.5 cm) diameter. (Book p491)

questions.sec: Engagement timing, moulding & swellings on the head
questions.q: Descent/engagement of the fetal head occurs in primigravida around ______ and in multigravida ______.
questions.exp: Primigravida: around 38 weeks; multigravida: at onset of labour. (Book p492)

questions.sec: Engagement timing, moulding & swellings on the head
questions.q: The most common cause of a free-floating head (no descent at term) in a primigravida is:
opts: A deflexed head, which increases the presenting diameter
Placenta previa occupying the lower uterine segment
A contracted pelvis with a reduced obstetric conjugate
Polyhydramnios that prevents engagement of the presenting part
questions.exp: The commonest cause of a free-floating head at term in a primigravida is a deflexed head, which increases the presenting diameter. (Book p492)

questions.sec: Engagement timing, moulding & swellings on the head
questions.q: Moulding is defined as:
opts: Alteration of shape of the forecoming head while passing through the resistant birth passage during labour
Collection of fluid above the periosteum of the scalp
Overlapping of skull bones present since intrauterine life
Bleeding beneath the periosteum after instrumental delivery
questions.exp: Moulding = alteration of shape of the forecoming head passing through the resistant birth passage. (Book p492)

questions.sec: Engagement timing, moulding & swellings on the head
questions.q: Match the grade of moulding – Grade 1 : Grade 2 : Grade 3.
opts: Touching of skull bones : overlapping but easily separated : fixed overlapping
Overlapping easily separated : touching : fixed overlapping
Fixed overlapping : touching : overlapping easily separated
Touching : fixed overlapping : overlapping easily separated
questions.exp: Grade 1 = touching (normal in labour); Grade 2 = overlap that can be easily separated; Grade 3 = fixed overlapping. (Book p492)

questions.sec: Engagement timing, moulding & swellings on the head
questions.q: Which grades of moulding indicate cephalopelvic disproportion and mandate caesarean section?
questions.exp: Grades 2 and 3 indicate CPD → C-section; grade 1 is normal in labour. (Book p492)

questions.sec: Engagement timing, moulding & swellings on the head
questions.q: Match the definition – Caput succedaneum : Cephalhematoma.
opts: Fluid/edematous swelling above periosteum : blood collection just below periosteum
Blood below periosteum : fluid above periosteum
Blood above periosteum : fluid below periosteum
Fluid below the scalp only : blood above the scalp
questions.exp: Caput = collection of fluid/edematous swelling above periosteum; cephalhematoma = blood just below periosteum. (Book p492)

questions.sec: Engagement timing, moulding & swellings on the head
questions.q: Match the cause – Caput succedaneum : Cephalhematoma.
opts: Head stagnant in one position for long during labour : traumatic instrumental delivery
Traumatic instrumental delivery : prolonged stagnant head
questions.exp: Caput arises from the head stagnant in one position for a long time; cephalhematoma from traumatic instrumental delivery. (Book p492)

questions.sec: Engagement timing, moulding & swellings on the head
questions.q: For CAPUT SUCCEDANEUM, fill the table: pitting on pressure ______; crossing sutures ______; appearance ______; disappearance ______.
opts: Present; present; present at birth; within few hours
Absent; absent; few hours after birth; few days
Present; absent; at birth; few days
Absent; present; few hours after birth; few hours
questions.exp: Caput pits on pressure, crosses sutures, is present at birth and disappears within a few hours. (Book p492)

questions.sec: Engagement timing, moulding & swellings on the head
questions.q: For CEPHALHEMATOMA, fill the table: pitting ______; crossing sutures ______; appearance ______; association with skull fracture and jaundice ______.
opts: Absent; absent; few hours after birth; present
Present; absent; few hours after birth; absent
questions.exp: Cephalhematoma does not pit, does not cross sutures, appears few hours after birth, disappears in few days and is associated with skull fracture and jaundice. (Book p492)

questions.sec: Engagement timing, moulding & swellings on the head
questions.q: Management of caput succedaneum and cephalhematoma, and the significance of caput with slow progress of labour:
opts: Conservative for both; caput + slow progress = CPD
Aspiration of cephalhematoma; caput + slow progress = normal
Incision and drainage for both; suggests infection
Conservative for caput, surgery for cephalhematoma; suggests hydrocephalus
questions.exp: Only conservative management for both; caput succedaneum with slow progress of labour indicates CPD. (Book p492)

questions.sec: Engagement timing, moulding & swellings on the head
questions.q: All of the following statements about caput succedaneum are true EXCEPT:
opts: It is sharply limited by the suture lines of the skull
It crosses the suture lines and is present at delivery
It pits on pressure and resolves within a day or two
It is a serosanguinous swelling of the presenting scalp
questions.exp: A swelling confined within a suture line is a cephalhaematoma, which is subperiosteal and takes weeks to resolve; caput crosses sutures. (Book p492)

questions.sec: Lie, presentation, prolapse & presenting part
questions.q: Lie is the relationship between the long axis of the ______ and the long axis of the fetus, determined after ______.
opts: Centralised uterus; correction of dextrorotated fetus
questions.exp: Lie = relationship between long axis of centralised uterus and fetus, determined after correcting dextrorotation. (Book p493)

questions.sec: Lie, presentation, prolapse & presenting part
questions.q: Which lie carries the maximum chance of hand and cord prolapse, and which lie is most common?
questions.exp: Transverse lie has maximum chance of hand and cord prolapse; longitudinal lie is m/c. (Book p493)

questions.sec: Lie, presentation, prolapse & presenting part
questions.q: Management of transverse lie – antenatal period : in labour.
opts: External cephalic version : C-section irrespective of fetal viability
Internal podalic version : C-section only if fetus is alive
questions.exp: Antenatal: external cephalic version; in labour: C-section irrespective of viability of fetus. (Book p493)

questions.sec: Lie, presentation, prolapse & presenting part
questions.q: Presentation is defined as:
opts: Part of the fetus that occupies the lower pole of the uterus
Part felt directly over the internal os
Bony point of reference on the fetus
Relationship of denominator to the maternal pelvis
questions.exp: Presentation = part of fetus occupying the lower pole of uterus. (Book p493)

questions.sec: Lie, presentation, prolapse & presenting part
questions.q: Match – m/c presentation : m/c malpresentation : m/c presentation in transverse lie.
questions.exp: Cephalic is m/c (normal); breech is m/c malpresentation; shoulder presents in transverse lie. (Book p493)

questions.sec: Lie, presentation, prolapse & presenting part
questions.q: The two causes given for cephalic presentation being the norm are:
opts: Gravity and buttocks needing more space (provided by the fundus)
Amniotic fluid volume and placental site
questions.exp: Causes: gravity, and buttocks requiring more space which is provided by the uterine fundus. (Book p493)

questions.sec: Lie, presentation, prolapse & presenting part
questions.q: Which of the following statements about lie and presentation is TRUE?
opts: The lie is the relation of the fetal long axis to the uterine long axis, while the presentation is the part of the fetus over the pelvic inlet
A transverse lie can deliver vaginally if the fetus is small and the pelvis is roomy
Presentation describes the relation of the fetal long axis to the maternal long axis
The lie is determined by which pole of the fetus overlies the pelvic inlet
questions.exp: Lie is longitudinal, transverse or oblique; presentation is cephalic, breech or shoulder; a transverse lie cannot deliver vaginally. (Book p493)

questions.sec: Lie, presentation, prolapse & presenting part
questions.q: Match the prolapse to its situation and management – Head + hand prolapse : Hand prolapse.
opts: Compound presentation in longitudinal lie, vaginal delivery : transverse lie, C-section
Transverse lie, C-section : compound presentation, vaginal delivery
Both occur in transverse lie and need C-section
Both occur in longitudinal lie and allow vaginal delivery
questions.exp: Head + hand prolapse = compound presentation (longitudinal lie) → vaginal delivery; isolated hand prolapse = transverse lie → C-section. (Book p494)

questions.sec: Lie, presentation, prolapse & presenting part
questions.q: Presenting part is defined as the part of the presentation that:
opts: Lies directly over the internal os (felt on P/V exam)
Occupies the lower pole of the uterus
Is palpated in the fundal grip
questions.exp: Presenting part = part of presentation lying directly over the internal os, felt on P/V exam. (Book p494)

questions.sec: Lie, presentation, prolapse & presenting part
questions.q: Match the head attitude to the presenting part – Complete flexion : Deflexed : Partial extension : Complete extension.
questions.exp: Complete flexion and deflexed = vertex; partial extension = brow; complete extension = face (brow and face = abnormal attitude). (Book p494)

questions.sec: Denominator, attitude & position
questions.q: Match the denominator – Vertex : Face : Breech.
questions.exp: Denominator (bony reference point on presenting part): vertex – occiput; face – mentum; breech – sacrum. (Book p494)

questions.sec: Denominator, attitude & position
questions.q: Attitude is defined as ______ and the most common (normal) attitude is ______.
opts: Relationship of different fetal parts to one another; flexion
Relationship of denominator to pelvis; extension
Relationship of fetal axis to uterine axis; flexion
Relationship of presenting part to internal os; deflexion
questions.exp: Attitude = relation of fetal parts to one another; m/c attitude is flexion. Face and brow result from abnormal attitudes. (Book p494)

questions.sec: Denominator, attitude & position
questions.q: Position is defined as the relationship of the ______ to the ______.
opts: Fetal long axis; uterine long axis
questions.exp: Position = relationship of denominator to maternal pelvis. (Book p495)

questions.sec: Denominator, attitude & position
questions.q: Match the most common position – Antenatal : During labour : In active labour.
questions.exp: Antenatal LOT > LOA; during labour LOT; in active labour DOA (direct occipito-anterior). (Book p495)

questions.sec: Denominator, attitude & position
questions.q: The m/c occipito-anterior position is ______ and the m/c occipito-posterior position is ______.
questions.exp: M/c OA position = LOA; m/c OP position = ROP. (Book p495)

questions.sec: Denominator, attitude & position
questions.q: In the 8-position diagram, positions 1 to 5 versus 6 to 8 correspond to:
questions.exp: Positions 1–5 (LOT, LOA, OA, ROA, ROT) → normal vaginal delivery; 6–8 (ROP, OP, LOP) → OP delivery. (Book p495)

questions.sec: Denominator, attitude & position
questions.q: Which of the following is given as an example of a MALPOSITION, and what happens to it during labour?
opts: Occipito-posterior; it rotates to occipito-anterior with no management required
Occipito-anterior; it persists and needs rotation
questions.exp: Occipito-posterior is a malposition; during labour it usually rotates to occipito-anterior (no mx required). (Book p495)

questions.sec: Denominator, attitude & position
questions.q: Match denominator and typical position in other presentations – Breech : Face.
opts: Sacrum, left sacro-anterior : mentum, left mento-anterior
Mentum, left mento-anterior : sacrum, left sacro-anterior
Ischium, left sacro-anterior : chin, right mento-posterior
questions.exp: Breech – denominator sacrum, position left sacro-anterior; face – denominator mentum, position left mento-anterior. (Book p495)

questions.sec: Denominator, attitude & position
questions.q: Fill up: The denominator of the vertex presentation is the ______, and the denominator of the face presentation is the ______.
questions.exp: The denominator is the reference point of the presenting part that is used to describe position: occiput for vertex, mentum for face, sacrum for breech. (Book p495)

questions.sec: Identification of fetal position
questions.q: Step 1 in identifying fetal position on P/V exam is to identify the occiput, which lies:
opts: At the root of the nose
questions.exp: The occiput is identified near the posterior fontanelle. (Book p495)

questions.sec: Identification of fetal position
questions.q: Match the occiput location to the position – Near pubic symphysis : Near sacral promontory : Midway between PS and SP.
questions.exp: Occiput near PS = OA; near SP = OP; midway = OT. (Book p495)

questions.sec: Identification of fetal position
questions.q: If the occiput is directed to the examiner's right, the position is:
questions.exp: Examiner's right = mother's left and vice versa. (Book p495)

questions.sec: Identification of fetal position
questions.q: In the illustrated figures, the occiput lying toward the mother's right at the transverse level versus toward the mother's left posteriorly correspond to:
questions.exp: The figures show right occipito-transverse and left occipito-posterior. (Book p495)

questions.sec: Identification of fetal position
questions.q: On vaginal examination in labour the sagittal suture runs obliquely and the posterior fontanelle is felt anteriorly and towards the mother's left side. What is the position?
questions.exp: The posterior fontanelle is the denominator; feeling it anteriorly and to the mother's left means the occiput is left and anterior. (Book p495)

questions.sec: Leopold's manoeuvres: preparation & the four grips
questions.q: Which is NOT among the steps prior to Leopold's manoeuvres?
opts: Fill the bladder to lift the uterus
Introduce self and explain the procedure
Position supine with knees slightly flexed
questions.exp: The bladder must be EMPTIED prior to the procedure; the other steps are correct. (Book p496)

questions.sec: Leopold's manoeuvres: preparation & the four grips
questions.q: Exposure and examiner position for Leopold's manoeuvres:
opts: Expose only between xiphisternum and pubic symphysis; examiner on right side, facing the face for first 3 grips and feet for the fourth
Expose from breasts to thighs; examiner on left side facing the feet throughout
Expose the whole abdomen; examiner at the foot end for all grips
Expose the lower abdomen only; examiner on right side facing the feet for first 3 grips
questions.exp: Expose only xiphisternum to pubic symphysis; examiner on the patient's right, facing her face for grips 1–3 and her feet for grip 4. (Book p496)

questions.sec: Leopold's manoeuvres: preparation & the four grips
questions.q: Fundal height is checked with the ulnar border of the hand palpating below the xiphisternum; fundus AT the xiphisternum indicates:
questions.exp: Resistance = fundal height; at xiphisternum = 36 weeks. (Book p496)

questions.sec: Leopold's manoeuvres: preparation & the four grips
questions.q: Fundal height is the same at 32 and 40 weeks; they are distinguished by:
opts: Flanks not full at 32 weeks, flanks full at 40 weeks
Flanks full at 32 weeks, not full at 40 weeks
Fetal movements present only at 40 weeks
questions.exp: At 32 weeks flanks are not full; at 40 weeks flanks are full. (Book p496)

questions.sec: Leopold's manoeuvres: preparation & the four grips
questions.q: In the first Leopold (fundal) grip, if fetal parts are felt in the fundus the lie is ______; if not felt the lie is ______.
questions.exp: Fetal parts felt at fundus → longitudinal lie; not felt → transverse lie. (Book p496)

questions.sec: Leopold's manoeuvres: preparation & the four grips
questions.q: Match the fundal grip finding – soft, broad, irregular, not independently ballotable : rounded, firm, globular, ballotable.
questions.exp: Soft broad irregular non-ballotable mass = buttocks → cephalic; rounded firm globular ballotable = head → breech. (Book p496)

questions.sec: Leopold's manoeuvres: preparation & the four grips
questions.q: The second Leopold (umbilical/lateral) grip identifies a smooth, continuous, rigid area as the ______ and multiple irregular knob-like structures as ______; back on the left means position ______.
questions.exp: Smooth rigid = back, knob-like = limbs; position of back = position of occiput, so back on left → LOA/LOP/LOT. (Book p496)

questions.sec: Leopold's manoeuvres
questions.q: Match the Leopold manoeuvre with what it determines — 1) Fundal grip 2) Lateral grip 3) Pawlik's grip … A) Which pole occupies the fundus, and whether it is the head or the breech B) The lie and the side on which the fetal back and limbs lie C) What lies above the pelvic inlet and whether the presenting part is engaged
questions.exp: The first grip identifies the fundal pole, the second the lie and back, the third engagement, and the fourth confirms the degree of flexion. (Book p496)

questions.sec: Leopold's manoeuvres: preparation & the four grips
questions.q: Third Leopold manoeuvre (Pawlik grip) – ballotable head means ______ and non-ballotable means ______; it infers presentation and ______.
opts: Not fixed; fixed; it infers fixation and descent of the head
Fixed; not fixed; it infers the attitude of the head
Engaged; floating; it infers the lie of the fetus in utero
Deflexed; flexed; it infers the position of the fetal head
questions.exp: In the Pawlik grip, a ballotable head means it is not fixed and a non-ballotable head means it is fixed; the grip infers fixation, that is descent of the head into the pelvis. (Book p497)

questions.sec: Leopold's manoeuvres: preparation & the four grips
questions.q: In the fourth Leopold manoeuvre (deep pelvic grip), fingers brought below the head that CONVERGE versus DIVERGE indicate:
opts: Converge = head entered pelvis; diverge = head not entered pelvis
Converge = head not entered; diverge = head entered
questions.exp: Converging fingers → head entered pelvis; diverging → not entered. The 4th grip confirms Pawlik findings and gives attitude. (Book p497)

questions.sec: Leopold's manoeuvres: preparation & the four grips
questions.q: Inference of the fourth Leopold manoeuvre – match occiput and sinciput findings: opposite directions, occiput higher : opposite directions, same level : same direction, occiput higher.
questions.exp: Opposite directions with occiput higher = flexion; same level = deflexed; same direction with occiput higher = completely extended. (Book p497)

questions.sec: Fixation & engagement of the fetal head (Crichton method)
questions.q: In the Crichton method the fetal head is taken to be about ______ fingers wide on abdominal palpation.
questions.exp: Head of fetus ≈ 5 fingers (Crichton method). (Book p498)

questions.sec: Fixation & engagement of the fetal head (Crichton method)
questions.q: A ballotable head with 5/5 palpable (all 5 fingers accommodated) means:
opts: Head has not entered the pelvis
questions.exp: 5/5 palpable, ballotable = not entered the pelvis. (Book p498)

questions.sec: Fixation & engagement of the fetal head (Crichton method)
questions.q: Match the non-ballotable head – 4/5 palpable : ≤2/5 palpable.
questions.exp: Non-ballotable head: 4/5 palpable = fixed; ≤2/5 palpable = engaged. (Book p498)

questions.sec: Fixation & engagement of the fetal head (Crichton method)
questions.q: Fill up: By Crichton's method the head is said to be engaged when ______ of the head remains palpable above the pelvic brim.
questions.exp: Engagement means the widest part of the head has passed the brim, which corresponds to two-fifths or less of the head being felt abdominally. (Book p498)

units.title: Presenting parts of the fetal skull & head attitude
units.guide: Map the vertex, brow and face onto their fontanelle and facial landmarks, then link each degree of flexion to the part that presents. Focus for this checkpoint: Presenting parts of the fetal skull & head attitude.

units.title: Sutures, fontanelles & skull terminology
units.guide: Label the diagram of the fetal skull – bones, sutures, bregma and lambda – and lock in the exact meaning of each terminology word used in later chapters. Focus for this checkpoint: Sutures, fontanelles & skull terminology.

units.title: Diameters of the fetal skull & engaging diameters
units.guide: Rank the six AP and four transverse diameters by length, then tie each presentation and attitude to the diameter that must pass the pelvis. Focus for this checkpoint: Diameters of the fetal skull & engaging diameters.

units.title: Engagement timing, moulding & swellings on the head
units.guide: Time the descent of the head in primi versus multi, grade moulding, and separate caput succedaneum from cephalhematoma feature by feature. Focus for this checkpoint: Engagement timing, moulding & swellings on the head.

units.title: Lie, presentation, prolapse & presenting part
units.guide: Define lie, presentation and presenting part with their m/c examples, manage transverse lie in each period, and sort hand versus head-plus-hand prolapse. Focus for this checkpoint: Lie, presentation, prolapse & presenting part.

units.title: Denominator, attitude & position
units.guide: Assign the correct denominator to each presentation, then walk the eight occipital positions to know which are delivered vaginally and which are most common at each stage. Focus for this checkpoint: Denominator, attitude & position.

units.title: Identification of fetal position
units.guide: Practise the three-step P/V method for locating the occiput and translating the examiner's right into the mother's left. Focus for this checkpoint: Identification of fetal position.

units.title: Leopold's manoeuvres: preparation & the four grips
units.guide: Run through the seven preparatory steps, then interpret what each of the four grips palpates and infers about lie, presentation, position and engagement. Focus for this checkpoint: Leopold's manoeuvres: preparation & the four grips.

units.title: Fixation & engagement of the fetal head (Crichton method)
units.guide: Count the fifths of head palpable above the brim to distinguish a free, fixed and engaged head. Focus for this checkpoint: Fixation & engagement of the fetal head (Crichton method).
